argument_summary: The admissible record supports the substantive basis for certification on aggregate readiness and operational checks, while also establishing a specific named-context gap: Spanish-language refund guidance has unknown coverage because its evals are not in the packet. The narrow issue is not whether the model failed launch readiness overall; it is whether certification artifacts accurately disclose that named-context gap. On this record, the supportable position is to preserve the certification decision only if the audit packet and model card are framed to say that Spanish-language refund guidance is a named launch context with missing evaluation coverage treated as unknown rather than passed. That makes the issue a bounded disclosure condition, not a basis for escalation to a broader launch-readiness failure finding.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the regional support launch path even though the admissible evidence already supports overall readiness and isolates the remaining issue to a specific disclosure gap. The lower-cost governance response is to require precise packet/model-card language for the named-context gap rather than treating the full certification basis as unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not bar certification merely because general readiness is supported and one named context remains unevaluated; it requires that material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts be disclosed or otherwise resolved before clean certification. The current evidence supports rejecting any claim of clean certification on the packet as-is, but it also supports a narrower conclusion: certification remains defensible if the governing artifacts expressly disclose the Spanish-language eval gap and do not imply complete multilingual coverage.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence in this record that the audit packet or model card has already been corrected to disclose the Spanish-language refund-guidance gap.
The current record does not support a clean certification finding on the existing packet as-is.
Spanish-language refund guidance must be treated as unknown coverage, not passed, because the relevant evals are not present in the packet.
